proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 追贈 is a posthumous office grant, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Duke Xu of Ancheng, son of Wuji, and Duke Lingxiu of Linru, son of Chang, were equally lavish; with Zhanzhi they competed in cuisine, furnishings, dress, and equipage.
proposals.after: He Xu, Duke of Ancheng, son of Wuji, and Meng Lingxiu, Duke of Linru, son of Chang, were equally lavish; with Zhanzhi they competed in cuisine, furnishings, dress, and equipage.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安成公何勖 is He Xu; English wrongly turns the surname into 'Duke Xu'.

proposals.before: Xu rose to Palace Attendant and was posthumously given the temple name Duke of Dissipation.
proposals.after: Xu rose to Palace Attendant and was posthumously given the posthumous name Duke of Dissipation.
proposals.reason: 諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.

proposals.before: Lingxiu was a master of pitch-pot and rose to Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Lingxiu was a master of the board game tanqi and rose to Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 彈棋 is the board game tanqi, not pitch-pot.

proposals.before: He had three sons: Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by Liu Shao.
proposals.after: Of his three sons, Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by Liu Shao.
proposals.reason: The colon listing reads as if only two sons exist; Hengzhi is the third, named next.

proposals.before: Dan's consort was Xu Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was his sister.
proposals.after: Dan's consort was Xu Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was Xu Zhanzhi's sister.
proposals.reason: 'his sister' is ambiguous; Chinese 湛妹 refers to Zhanzhi's sister.

decisions.reason: 追贈中書侍郎 is a posthumous grant of office; enfeoffment (封) is not in the Chinese, and the proposed wording matches the sense.
安成公何勖 and 臨汝公孟靈休 name He Xu and Meng Lingxiu; ‘Duke Xu’ and ‘Duke Lingxiu’ wrongly treat personal names as surnames/titles.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安成公何勖……臨汝公孟靈休

decisions.reason: 追諡荒公 awards a posthumous name (諡); temple name (廟號) is a different category and is not present here.
彈棋 is the board game tanqi; pitch-pot is 投壺 and is not the game named here.
三子：聿之、謙之，為元凶所殺 names only two of the three sons as killed; the colon-list English wrongly implies the roster is complete in this sentence, while 恆之 follows in s0132.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三子：聿之、謙之，為元凶所殺

decisions.reason: 鑠妃即湛妹 makes Shuo’s consort Zhanzhi’s sister; ‘his sister’ could be read as Dan’s or Shuo’s sister, so naming Xu Zhanzhi removes the ambiguity.
